headline: Application Development
description: Full-stack development from first principles. We cover the modern web stack — TypeScript, React, Next.js, NestJS, and the deployment pipeline that takes your app to production.

tools.name: TypeScript
tools.definition: Typed superset of JavaScript — catch errors before runtime and build large codebases with confidence.

tools.name: JavaScript
tools.definition: The language of the web — runs in every browser and on the server via Node.js.

tools.name: Python
tools.definition: General-purpose scripting language — excellent for backend APIs, automation, and data tasks alongside web apps.

tools.name: React
tools.definition: UI component library from Meta — the most popular way to build interactive web interfaces.

tools.name: Next.js
tools.definition: React framework for production — adds routing, SSR, and API routes out of the box.

tools.name: next/og
tools.definition: Next.js built-in for generating dynamic Open Graph images — renders JSX to a PNG via ImageResponse, runs on the edge.

tools.name: Vue
tools.definition: Progressive frontend framework — gentle learning curve with a clean, approachable syntax.

tools.name: Svelte
tools.definition: Compiler-based UI framework — writes less code, ships no runtime, blazing fast results.

tools.name: Vite
tools.definition: Lightning-fast dev server and build tool — replaces Webpack with near-instant hot reload.

tools.name: Tailwind CSS
tools.definition: Utility-first CSS framework — style directly in HTML with atomic classes, no context switching.

tools.name: Framer Motion
tools.definition: Production-ready animation library for React — declarative animations with physics-based springs.

tools.name: PostCSS
tools.definition: CSS transformation tool — processes your stylesheets through plugins like autoprefixer and Tailwind at build time.

tools.name: Lucide React
tools.definition: Open-source icon library for React — clean, consistent SVG icons as components, tree-shakeable and typed.

tools.name: Simple Icons
tools.definition: Free SVG icons for popular brands — over 3,000 logos with consistent style, great for tech stack displays.

tools.name: Storybook
tools.definition: UI component workshop — build, document, and test components in isolation before wiring them up.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.definition: JavaScript runtime for servers — run JS outside the browser to build APIs and CLI tools.

tools.name: NestJS
tools.definition: Opinionated Node.js framework — brings structure and TypeScript-first patterns to backend APIs.

tools.name: FastAPI
tools.definition: Python API framework — auto-generates docs, validates requests, and runs at async speed.

tools.name: Express
tools.definition: Minimal Node.js web framework — the building block behind most Node APIs, unopinionated by design.

tools.name: Hono
tools.definition: Ultra-lightweight web framework — runs on any JS runtime including Cloudflare Workers and Bun.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.definition: The most powerful open-source SQL database — handles complex queries, JSON, and scales well.

tools.name: MySQL
tools.definition: The world's most-used open-source database — fast, reliable, and the backbone of most web apps.

tools.name: MongoDB
tools.definition: Document database — stores JSON-like objects, great for flexible schemas and rapid iteration.

tools.name: Redis
tools.definition: In-memory key-value store — used for caching, sessions, and real-time pub/sub messaging.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.definition: Open-source Firebase alternative — PostgreSQL database with auth, storage, and realtime out of the box.

tools.name: Prisma
tools.definition: Type-safe ORM for Node.js — write database queries in TypeScript with full autocomplete support.

tools.name: Drizzle
tools.definition: Lightweight TypeScript ORM — SQL-like syntax with zero runtime overhead and schema-first approach.

tools.name: Zod
tools.definition: TypeScript-first schema validation — define your data shapes once, validate everywhere at runtime.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.definition: Deployment platform for frontend apps — git push and your Next.js app is live in seconds.

tools.name: Docker
tools.definition: Containerisation tool — package your app and its dependencies so it runs identically anywhere.

tools.name: Railway
tools.definition: Simple cloud platform — deploy databases and backends from GitHub with zero infrastructure config.

tools.name: AWS
tools.definition: Amazon's cloud — the industry standard for scalable, production-grade infrastructure at any scale.

tools.name: Clerk
tools.definition: Drop-in authentication for React — user management, sessions, and MFA in minutes, not days.

tools.name: NextAuth
tools.definition: Auth library for Next.js — handles OAuth providers, sessions, and JWT out of the box.

tools.name: JWT
tools.definition: JSON Web Token — a compact, self-contained token for securely passing user identity between services.

tools.name: bcrypt
tools.definition: Password hashing library — salts and hashes passwords with a cost factor so brute-force attacks are computationally expensive.

tools.name: REST
tools.definition: Standard architecture for HTTP APIs — resources mapped to URLs with predictable CRUD operations.

tools.name: GraphQL
tools.definition: Query language for APIs — clients request exactly the data they need, nothing more.

tools.name: tRPC
tools.definition: End-to-end type-safe APIs — share types between your Next.js frontend and backend with no schema files.

tools.name: Jest
tools.definition: JavaScript testing framework — write unit and integration tests with a simple, familiar API.

tools.name: Vitest
tools.definition: Fast unit test framework powered by Vite — drop-in Jest replacement with native ESM support.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.definition: Browser automation and end-to-end testing — simulate real user interactions across all major browsers.

tools.name: Algolia
tools.definition: Hosted search-as-a-service — fast, typo-tolerant full-text search with a generous free tier and a Next.js SDK.

tools.name: Typesense
tools.definition: Open-source alternative to Algolia — self-hostable or cloud, great for large guide and content libraries.

tools.name: Orama
tools.definition: Edge-native full-text search — runs client-side or at the edge, has a Vercel integration, and handles vector search.

tools.name: Git
tools.definition: Version control system — track every change to your codebase and collaborate without stepping on toes.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.definition: Cloud platform for Git repositories — pull requests, issues, Actions, and the world's largest code community.

tools.name: Postman
tools.definition: API testing client — send requests, inspect responses, and document your API without writing code.

tools.name: pnpm
tools.definition: Fast, disk-efficient package manager — installs node_modules up to 3x faster than npm.

tools.name: Turborepo
tools.definition: Monorepo build system — caches tasks and runs pipelines in parallel across your workspace.

tools.name: marked
tools.definition: Fast, lightweight markdown parser for Node.js — converts .md files to HTML with zero dependencies.

tools.name: Fuse.js
tools.definition: Lightweight fuzzy-search library — no server required, searches arrays of objects client-side with weighted keys and configurable threshold.

tools.name: clsx
tools.definition: Tiny utility for constructing class name strings — conditionally join Tailwind classes without messy template literals.

tools.name: ESLint
tools.definition: JavaScript and TypeScript linter — catches bugs, enforces style rules, and keeps code consistent across a team.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.definition: AI pair programmer in your editor — autocompletes code and writes functions from comments.

tools.name: Claude
tools.definition: Anthropic's AI — strong at code review, architecture planning, and writing clean, documented code.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.definition: AI-first code editor — built on VS Code with deep Claude/GPT integration for chat-driven development.
